Create two synthetic genes with the same expected RNA abundance, sample old and
new molecules, and use the sampled population to initialize a perturbation. You
can also generate the labeling likelihood files used for fitting.

| To get | Use |
|---|---|
| Counts for one parameter set | `simulate_distr_total()` |
| Counts for multiple genes in a `grandR` object | `simulateBursting()` |
| Simulated labeling evidence and files for fitting | `SimulateReads()` |
| Paths to the generated files | `simulation_files()` |

> The count examples run during rendering. Run the final labeling-evidence
> example in R to write files to a temporary directory.

```{r packages}
library(buRst)
library(grandR)
```

## 1. Draw a steady-state population

Burst initiation and degradation rates use the reciprocal time unit of the
labeling interval. Here, time is in hours. Both genes have expected steady-state
RNA abundance `km * B / d = 4`, but their burst frequencies and sizes differ.

```{r define-truth}
truth <- data.frame(
  gene = c("frequent_small", "rare_large"),
  km = c(2, 0.5), B = c(1, 4), d = c(0.5, 0.5)
)
truth$expected_mean <- with(truth, km * B / d)
knitr::kable(truth, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Gene", "Frequency", "Size", "Degradation", "Expected mean"))
```

```{r simulate-reference}
reference <- simulateBursting(
  kms = truth$km, Bs = truth$B, ds = truth$d,
  gene.info = truth$gene,
  t.end = 1, no.cells = 120,
  condition = "reference", tp.label = 0,
  ntr.sim = FALSE, steady = TRUE,
  parallel = FALSE, seed = 1, on_gene_error = "stop"
)
counts <- as.matrix(grandR::GetMatrix(reference, mode.slot = "count"))
new <- as.matrix(grandR::GetMatrix(reference, mode.slot = "new"))
old <- as.matrix(grandR::GetMatrix(reference, mode.slot = "old"))
stopifnot(all(counts == new + old))
```

With `ntr.sim = FALSE`, the object contains true simulated `count`, `new`, `old`
and `ntr` slots. It has no noisy labeling evidence and does not write an HDF5 file.

```{r summarize-counts}
summary_counts <- data.frame(
  gene = truth$gene,
  sample_mean = rowMeans(counts),
  sample_variance = apply(counts, 1, var),
  zero_fraction = rowMeans(counts == 0)
)
knitr::kable(summary_counts, digits = 3,
             col.names = c("Gene", "Sample mean", "Variance", "Fraction with no RNA"))
```

```{r plot-counts, fig.cap="Simulated cell-level counts for two genes with the same expected abundance. Sampling variability makes their observed means differ."}
set.seed(2)
boxplot(t(counts), names = c("Frequent / small", "Rare / large"),
        col = c("#B4D6E0", "#F5C6B8"), outline = FALSE,
        ylab = "RNA molecules per cell", las = 1)
stripchart(lapply(seq_len(nrow(counts)), function(i) counts[i, ]),
           method = "jitter", vertical = TRUE, add = TRUE,
           pch = 16, cex = 0.4,
           col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#243344", alpha.f = 0.4))
```

The true parameter values are attached to the gene information, using the
suffix selected by `tp.label`:

```{r inspect-truth}
grandR::GeneInfo(reference)[, c("Gene", "true_km.t0", "true_B.t0", "true_d.t0")]
```

## 2. Change the kinetics at labeling onset

A transient simulation starts with the molecules already present. Supply the
reference **total counts** as `init`. Rows must follow the same gene order and
columns must match `no.cells`.

Here, the first gene doubles its burst frequency and the second doubles its
burst size. Degradation remains unchanged.

```{r simulate-perturbation}
truth$km_after <- truth$km * c(2, 1)
truth$B_after <- truth$B * c(1, 2)
truth$d_after <- truth$d
truth$true_log2FC_km <- log2(truth$km_after / truth$km)
truth$true_log2FC_B <- log2(truth$B_after / truth$B)

perturbed <- simulateBursting(
  kms = truth$km_after, Bs = truth$B_after, ds = truth$d_after,
  gene.info = truth$gene,
  t.end = 1, no.cells = ncol(counts),
  condition = "perturbed", tp.label = 1,
  steady = FALSE, init = counts,
  ntr.sim = FALSE, parallel = FALSE,
  seed = 2, on_gene_error = "stop"
)
knitr::kable(truth[, c("gene", "true_log2FC_km", "true_log2FC_B")])
```

The new condition evolves from the reference population for one hour. Its
observed mean is generally not yet the mean of the new steady state.

```{r transient-means}
after_counts <- as.matrix(grandR::GetMatrix(perturbed, mode.slot = "count"))
expected_after <- with(truth,
  km_after * B_after / d_after +
    (expected_mean - km_after * B_after / d_after) * exp(-d_after)
)
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  gene = truth$gene,
  reference_sample_mean = rowMeans(counts),
  perturbed_sample_mean = rowMeans(after_counts),
  expected_population_mean_after_1h = expected_after
), digits = 3)
```

The theoretical mean above averages over the reference population. A finite
simulated sample also has sampling variability in its initial counts.

## 3. Generate labeling likelihoods

The count slots above give you the simulated truth. A fit to experimental data
uses the conversion evidence because the true new-RNA count in each cell is
unknown. `SimulateReads()` adds that layer and exports the full discrete
likelihoods. Here we generate evidence for the perturbed condition.

```{r simulate-evidence, eval=FALSE}
work <- tempfile("buRst_example_")
dir.create(work)

with_reads <- SimulateReads(
  perturbed, output_prefix = file.path(work, "perturbed"),
  p.old = 1e-4, p.new = 0.04, fit.beta = FALSE,
  burstMCMC = FALSE, parallel = FALSE, seed = 4
)
simulation_files(with_reads)
```

Keep the returned `grandR` object with the count, gene and cell reference files
and `4sU.Binom.discrete.h5` in the generated `.targets` directory. Set
`fit.beta = TRUE` if you also need the `alpha` and `beta` slots for the beta
approximation.

| Fitting function | Labeling input |
|---|---|
| `fit_gene()` | Full discrete likelihood in HDF5 |
| `fit_gene_MAP()` | Estimated new RNA treated as exact |
| `fit_gene_beta()` | Per-cell beta approximation |
| `fit_gene_truth()` | Simulated true new and old counts |

**Continue with** the [acute-perturbation experiment](acute_pertubation.html) to
combine two conditions, fit the full likelihood, and compare estimates with
the known changes.
